tasks.title: Migrate test-validator.ts to defensive I/O
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/test-validator.test.ts with failing tests: (a) malformed tasks.json (missing comma) is recovered via readTasksFile; validateTaskTests runs the test command and still writes back via writeTasksFile; (b) when readTasksFile throws TasksFileError (both parse AND snapshot fail), validateTaskTests returns { status: 'error', message } rather than crashing — preserve the existing ValidationResult return-shape contract; (c) snapshotTasksFile is called after each write (spy on it). Step 2: migrate src/test-validator.ts. Replace the bare 'JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))' at line ~70 with readTasksFile from src/tasks-file.ts; replace the writeFileSync calls (at lines ~86, ~93, ~102 — three timeout/can't-run/revert paths) with writeTasksFile plus snapshotTasksFile. Preserve the appendNote semantics exactly (append with ' | ' separator). Do NOT change the ValidationResult enum or the CANT_RUN_PATTERNS list. Make new tests pass without regressing existing validator tests.
tasks.notes: TDD applied strictly. Added 3 failing tests to test/test-validator.test.ts under a new 'defensive I/O' describe block — confirmed all 3 fail against the old impl (SyntaxError on malformed JSON, ENOENT on missing file, spy never called). Then migrated src/test-validator.ts: imported * as tasksFileModule + named TasksFileError; replaced JSON.parse(readFileSync) at line ~70 with tasksFileModule.readTasksFile({ dataDir: path.dirname(tasksFilePath) }) wrapped in try/catch — on TasksFileError returns { status: 'error', message: err.message }, non-TasksFileError rethrows; replaced all three writeFileSync calls with a writeAndSnapshot helper that does writeTasksFile + snapshotTasksFile. appendNote semantics (' | ' separator) preserved verbatim; ValidationResult enum and CANT_RUN_PATTERNS untouched. Full suite: 640 → 643 (3 added, 0 regressed). Wrinkles for next agent (task #10 archiver): (1) chose path.dirname(tasksFilePath) as dataDir rather than adding a new opt — keeps ValidateTaskTestsOpts contract unchanged; matches the existing run.ts convention where tasks.json and .ralph_tasks_snapshot.json live in the same dir. Archiver is already called with an explicit dataDir opt at src/commands/run.ts:275 so it can pass through as-is. (2) Used 'import * as tasksFileModule' + 'tasksFileModule.snapshotTasksFile(...)' namespace-style calls in impl so spyOn(tasksFileModule, 'snapshotTasksFile') works across modules in Bun — same pattern tasks-file.test.ts uses to spy on fs.writeFileSync. If task #10 wants to spy on readTasksFile/writeTasksFile/snapshotTasksFile from task-archiver.ts, apply the same import pattern. (3) Small helper writeAndSnapshot() de-duplicates the 3 write sites; feel free to inline if preferred, but it also guarantees snapshot-after-write ordering for task (c).

tasks.title: Migrate task-archiver.ts + stop silent swallowing
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/task-archiver.test.ts with failing tests: (a) archiver uses readTasksFile so corrupted tasks.json can be repaired and archival proceeds normally; (b) when readTasksFile throws TasksFileError, the archiver returns { archivedCount: 0, prevNotes: null, warnings: [<string>] } AND appends an entry to <dataDir>/corruption.log AND appends a line to the iteration log (pass iterationLogPath into archiveCompletedTasks opts if not already present). Current behavior silently swallows parse errors (src/task-archiver.ts:27-31) — the new test must catch that and require it be surfaced. Step 2: migrate src/task-archiver.ts. Add a 'warnings: string[]' field to the ArchiveResult type. Replace the try/catch at lines 27-31 with a readTasksFile call; on TasksFileError, push a descriptive message to warnings AND log to the iteration log (and corruption.log is already written by readTasksFile); replace every JSON.stringify+writeFileSync pair with writeTasksFile + snapshotTasksFile. Document in task notes the choice of warnings[] over an onError callback (simpler test harness, easier to assert on). Make new tests pass without regressing existing archiver tests.

tasks.title: Migrate run.ts reads + snapshot + corruption counter + tempfile cleanup
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: extend test/commands/run.test.ts with failing tests covering: (a) main-loop read at src/commands/run.ts:445 goes through readTasksFile; (b) post-task-review status re-read at src/commands/run.ts:571 goes through readTasksFile; (c) a corruptionEvents counter initialised to 0 increments by 1 whenever readTasksFile returns repaired:true or restored:true anywhere it's called in runRun; (d) the final summary (src/commands/run.ts:610-619 block) emits a new line exactly '⚠ N corruption events recovered this run — see <dataDir>/corruption.log' ONLY when N > 0; when N === 0 the line is absent; (e) the ntfy notification body includes the corruption count when config.narration.ntfyTopic is set; (f) after the main-loop read succeeds, snapshotTasksFile is called (per-iteration snapshot); (g) the TEMP_FILES cleanup at src/commands/run.ts:345 is extended to glob-sweep files matching .ralph_task_<id>_notes.md under dataDir at run end — use fs.readdirSync(dataDir).filter(f => /^\.ralph_task_\d+_notes\.md$/.test(f)) rather than importing a glob library. Step 2: implement all seven in src/commands/run.ts. Make all new tests pass without regressing existing run tests.

tasks.title: Tighten post-task-reviewer path-scoped allowlist
tasks.description: TDD in one task. Step 1: add a failing assertion to test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts using the existing mock-spawn pattern. Find the test that captures the args array passed to spawn by spawnPostTaskReviewer. Add an assertion that the args array contains '--allowedTools' immediately followed by the EXACT string 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit(.ralph/review-post.md),Write(.ralph/review-post.md)'. The current production value at src/post-task-reviewer.ts:124 is 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write' — confirm the test fails against the current value (that's the TDD verification). Step 2: change the --allowedTools value in src/post-task-reviewer.ts:119-129 from 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write' to 'Read,Glob,Grep,Edit(.ralph/review-post.md),Write(.ralph/review-post.md)'. This activates Claude Code's path-scoped allowlist enforcement (verified April 2026 — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md): Edit and Write outside .ralph/review-post.md will be denied before hitting disk. No other changes to the file. Make the new test pass without regressing any other post-task-reviewer tests.

tasks.title: Tighten post-task-reviewer prompt (belt-and-suspenders)
tasks.description: Add an explicit rule near the top of agents/post-task-reviewer.md: a new line stating 'You may only write to .ralph/review-post.md — never modify .ralph/tasks.json.' This is defense-in-depth alongside the path-scoped allowlist from task 12 (the allowlist is the authoritative enforcement; the prompt keeps the agent from even trying). Preserve the existing '## Output Format' and '## Coverage Diagram' sections verbatim — do not reword or restructure them. Smoke-read the file after editing to confirm it still reads as a coherent agent prompt (no orphaned fragments, no broken section headers).

tasks.title: Document ralph task workflow in CLAUDE.md
tasks.description: Add a short 4-6 line section to CLAUDE.md under the 'Conventions' section (or a new 'Agent workflow' subsection if cleaner) explaining: agents must use the ralph task subcommand group (start, complete, note, set-status, add, show) for every mutation of .ralph/tasks.json; direct Edit/Write on .ralph/tasks.json is forbidden and is caught by the per-agent prompt ban plus the path-scoped allowlist on the post-task reviewer; the CLI ensures atomic writes and JSON validity so corruption becomes structurally impossible via this path. Keep the addition tight — do not rewrite the existing 'Architecture' or 'Key design patterns' sections; only add the new guidance.

tasks.title: Full-suite verification + build + manual corruption-recovery smoke test
tasks.description: Final verification task. Step 1: run 'bun test' — full suite must pass green. Step 2: run 'bun run build' — must produce a fresh dist/ralph without errors. Step 3: manual checks on a scratch project (create a throwaway dir with a hand-written tasks.json): (3a) run 'ralph task start 1 --iteration 1' then 'ralph task complete 1 --iteration 1 --notes "manual smoke"' then 'ralph task note 1 "appended"' then 'ralph task note 1 --replace "replaced"' — after each command, cat tasks.json and verify it parses as valid JSON. (3b) Deliberately break tasks.json (delete a comma after a notes field in any task); run 'ralph run' on the scratch project for one iteration; verify readTasksFile recovered via jsonrepair (look for the success path continuing) and that <dataDir>/corruption.log contains a new entry with stage:'jsonrepair'. (3c) Delete BOTH tasks.json AND .ralph/.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json; run 'ralph run' — verify TasksFileError is surfaced (not a silent failure) and the corruption.log entry records the complete fail. (3d) In a separate scratch repo with review.postTask enabled, trigger a post-task review and verify the reviewer cannot Edit .ralph/tasks.json — the Edit call should be denied by Claude Code's path-scoped allowlist; confirm by reading the stream-json output for a permission_denied event. Record all four results in the task's notes on completion. If any step fails, leave the task in-progress and document the failure in notes for the next iteration.
